question_text: What does the Bill of Rights protect?
disambiguation: Notice: it protects the rights of everyone living in the United States — not only citizens.

official_answers.text: (The basic) rights of people living in the United States
key_elements: rights of people in the United States

why_it_matters.text: The Bill of Rights flips the usual question. Instead of listing what people may do, it lists what the government may NOT do to them — like silence your speech or your religion. These are freedoms no leader can take away.

fun_fact.text: Our famous First Amendment — free speech and religion — was almost the Third! Twelve changes were proposed; the first two didn't pass back then, so number three jumped to the top. Even our rights were chosen one by one.

mnemonic.hook: The Bill of Rights is the first TEN amendments — and you have ten fingers.
mnemonic.link_sentence: Count the Bill of Rights on your hands: ten amendments, ten fingers.
